text: Henryk Rolirad (11 April 1909 – 4 January 1984) was a Polish food–systems engineer recognized as a Righteous among the Nations for saving Jews during World War II. Born in Poznań, Poland, he was adopted at age two by Stanisław and Stefania Rolirad. He graduated from Poznań's University of Economics and initially worked at a local Crafts Chamber before becoming director of the Poznań branch of the Polish travel agency Orbis. In 1938, Rolirad established an Orbis bureau in Zbąszyń. That same year, Nazi Germany deported many Polish–Jewish emigres back to Poland, and Rolirad began assisting these emigres arriving in Zbąszyń even before World War II began. During the German occupation, he was a member of the Polish Home Army's Security Corps and collaborated with the Jewish Military Union (Żydowski Związek Wojskowy) operating in the Warsaw Ghetto, supplying Jews with food, medicines, and forged documents both inside and outside the Ghetto, and providing his own home as a temporary refuge for Jews escaping the Ghetto. He also rented at least three other houses to hide Jews. On 23 April 1943, while sheltering Jews in one of his homes, Rolirad was captured by the German Gestapo. In German-occupied Poland, helping Jews was punishable by death. The Gestapo placed Rolirad and two Jewish women in a truck; during transit, the truck stopped at an intersection, and a Gestapo officer left to enter a nearby house, leaving only two guards. A member of the Polish underground resistance, unable to see who was inside, threw a hand grenade into the truck, seriously injuring Rolirad, who remained disabled for the rest of his life. In 1944, Rolirad met Maria Einstein, both originally from Poznań; they had previously met while helping Jews in Zbąszyń, and Rolirad saved her life. After the war, Rolirad married Maria Einstein. In 1965, they emigrated to Israel with their daughters and settled in Ramat Gan. Rolirad died on 4 January 1984 from a malignant illness and was interred at the Jaffa Catholic Cemetery in Tel Aviv. On 18 October 1966, Yad Vashem in Jerusalem recognized Henryk Rolirad as a Righteous among the Nations.
